Where it began

Kannaur Lokesh Rahul was born in Bengaluru on 18 April 1992 and grew up in Surathkal, near Mangalore. He began proper cricket training at ten, and within a couple of years was turning out for clubs in both Mangalore and Bangalore.

At 18 he moved to Bangalore for university and for cricket, and he was soon playing for Karnataka. In the 2014–15 season he made 337 against Uttar Pradesh, the first triple hundred anyone had scored for the state.

The player

His Test debut came in the Boxing Day Test at Melbourne in 2014. A quiet start was followed straight away by a maiden hundred at Sydney, and he has not stopped collecting them since. By October 2026 he had played 70 Tests and made 4,288 runs at 36.65, with 12 hundreds and 21 fifties.

The best of them is 199 against England, a single short of a double. He made 129 at Lord's in 2021, 123 in South Africa later that year, and in the 2025 series in England he scored 532 runs with two centuries. He has led India in three Tests, winning two, and in May 2026 he was named Test vice-captain.

What made him special

Rahul bats with a stillness that makes hard things look easy. On the 2021 tour of England he showed a lovely knack for knowing which balls to leave alone, and for waiting on the rest. He is also wonderfully adaptable: opener, number three, middle order, and on one tour in Sri Lanka a stand-in wicketkeeper as well.

If there is a gentle complaint, it is that he has been asked to move up and down the order so often that his figures have had to keep up with him. A Test average in the mid-thirties sells short a man who, on his day, looks like the best-organised batsman in the side. He also held a fair few catches, 81 in the field by October 2026.

Beyond the Tests

He has also been a fixture of India's white-ball teams. He was the first Indian to make a century on ODI debut, and he has been part of sides that won the Asia Cup in 2018 and 2023 and the Champions Trophy in 2025.

In the Indian Premier League he won the Orange Cap in 2020 with 670 runs, and in 2026 he became the first Indian to pass 150 in an IPL innings, an unbeaten 152 for Delhi Capitals. In 2023 he married the actress Athiya Shetty.

And finally

For a man who has made a triple hundred in the Ranji Trophy and a double-hundred-in-all-but-name against England, the 199 must still nag a little. It leaves something to aim for, and with his patience it would be no surprise to see him get there one day.
